title: Outbound delivery is confirmed by receipt readback
summary: After an outward message send, delivery is established by reading back the platform's own receipt for the exact target; an ambiguous send outcome is reconciled first and never repeated automatically.

protected.asset: The owner's outward communication channels and their reputation with counterparties
protected.failure: A send with an ambiguous outcome is retried blindly and produces duplicate external messages, or a failed send is reported as delivered.

rationale: A send call returning is not delivery evidence: transports can accept and then drop, time out after actual delivery, or deliver without the caller observing the receipt. The platform's own record — the message identifier present in the target thread, or its absence on readback — is the deciding evidence. Repeating a non-idempotent external action whose outcome is unknown risks a duplicate that cannot be unsent, so reconciliation of the exact target and any existing receipt always precedes a retry, and the retry path is bounded and visible.

variants.description: After each send, read the target thread or delivery surface and record the platform-assigned identifier of the exact message; only that readback closes the delivery.
When the send outcome is ambiguous, hold; reconcile the exact target and existing receipts; retry only through a bounded, human-visible path.

verification.method: Send a synthetic message to a test target, read back its platform identifier, then simulate an ambiguous failure and confirm no automatic repeat occurs and the held state names the exact target.
verification.evidence: The platform message identifier and target captured on readback, plus the held state of the ambiguous case; no message content.

rollback.method: Disable the readback requirement to restore send-and-trust behaviour; no state is mutated by readback itself.
rollback.safety: Readback is a read-only operation against the platform.

failure_modes: A send-call success return is logged as delivery proof.
An ambiguous timeout triggers an automatic duplicate send.
Readback against the wrong thread clears a message that never arrived.

hermes_versions.notes: Operational practice control: the range records the builds whose messaging delivery surfaces the procedure was read against, not a versioned platform feature.

last_verification.notes: General operational synthesis from recorded practice with private detail removed; the cited API documents a receipt surface, not an incident.

references: Telegram Bot API, sendMessage returns the sent Message object: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendmessage
General operational synthesis from recorded practice; no publicly verifiable incident is cited.
